Theme

Latin word

magister

magister, magistrī m.

noun, second declension

the director (of a company), the head; a master, the one in charge; a teacher; the head of a company, a society or a guild; teacher

In this lexicon

  • director

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.9.2: quī est magister in eā societāte; Cic. Planc. 32: plūrimārum magister; Levi–Bini p. 21; M-O s.v. corporation: president of a corporation, CEO

  • master

    also used · classical · Col. 1.18: magister operārum, an overseer (Lewis & Short); Cic. de Or. 1.244: puerī apud magistrōs exercentur (Lewis & Short)

  • president

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Planc. 32: maximārum societātum auctor, plūrimārum magister; M-O s.v. corporation: president of a corporation: societātis magister; Traupman 289

  • teacher

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 32, 169, 391; Traupman 338
